notes.title: 1.126 - The "oops I introduced a load of bugs with the last patch" patch
notes.content: [p]As proud as I was of the save slot system I introduced in the last patch, the general overhaul of various underlying components led to a few bugs that left the game in a rather broken state. [/p][p]Due to a lot of real-life chaos going on, and the fact that I'm the only person testing the game, I didn't actually realise just how broken it was.  [/p][p]If you discovered these bugs, or have now realised that your playthrough's reality has been utterly warped by the bugs in question (which allowed save data to persist when loading during an active session), then I can only apologise.  [/p][p]Hopefully I've squashed the biggest bugs now though. Hopefully. Fingers crossed.[/p]

notes.title: Version 1.125
notes.content:
This patch contains a few quality of life features, including:
[list]
[*]Save slots! You can now maintain up to 8 different saves for abundant save-scumming.
[*]Fixes for scrolling issues when returning from menus.
[*]A new dynamic spacer so that text tries to avoid bottoming out based on the size of the added text.
[*]The "logmode" feature is now partially on by default - meaning the game will tell you what it thought you meant when it detects a typo and tries to figure it out.
[/list]

Additionally, there's a one-line code fix for a bug that slipped into the last patch, in which it was possible to become a little bit unstuck in time due to certain timed events and effects persisting across saves. Oops!

notes.title: Major journal bug found - Patch pending...
notes.content:
Due to the entire rebuild of the save/load system to solve a possible security vulnerability, it seems that I've introduced a rather major bug, resulting in journal entries being incorrectly loaded.

I'm working on a fix right now. Unfortunately, it seems that saving a loaded game compounds the error; baking the messed up journal entries.

EDIT: A single line of important code has been deployed. The patch should be live before the day is out.

I apologise for any inconvenience.

notes.title: Security vulnerability fix
notes.content:
[h1]Oops[/h1]
I must offer my apologies to the one or two people who might actually be playing the game at the moment - I have nuked your save.
This was unavoidable. Due to the manner in which nerds fail to communicate rather important things to the wider world, it came to my attention rather late that my save system - which utilised something called the binary formatter - was potentially unsafe and relied upon technical things that will probably be deprecated in future software in general. Put simply, the way it read data from the save put users at potential risk from code injection - though this risk would only exist if you were downloading someone else's save file from nefarious sources on the internet.
So, a minimal edge-case risk, but still one I could not allow.

[h1]Silver Lining[/h1]
The save system now uses a more flexible xml-based solution, which not only means the game is actually more future proofed than before (technical anecdote - it uses a "var heap" system I created that dynamically populates itself by the very act of asking the value of a variable, meaning that loading an old save in a new version will not be a problem), it also means that if your save gets damaged somehow by my coding incompetence, it's actually possible to simply open the save in a text editor and manually modify values.
Of course, I do not advise doing this unless a specific fix is required - yes, it's possible to give yourself a pile of money. Yes, this will also break quest progression spectacularly.

[h1]Introducing the NB Book Binder[/h1]
In other news, a certain secondary program of mine is currently awaiting review by the powers that be. A by-product of my work on the game and the books, it is a tool that would allow anyone to package their own literary works using the same engine, replete with audio book support. If it is given the go-ahead, it will cost very little, and is rather cool. Watch this space.
